problem: Existing embodied navigation surveys reflect the priorities of their home fields: CV surveys cover language/social tasks under idealized state and action assumptions, robotics surveys cover sensing and SLAM, and neuromorphic surveys cover bio-inspired mechanisms. No unifying structure integrates sensing, social and motion intelligence.
motivation: Embodied navigation combines egocentric perception, high-level human instruction understanding and adaptive motion skills, but the literature is fragmented across CV, classic robotics and bionics. A single formulation is needed to place work from all fields in one map and to expose open problems.
key_idea: Formulate embodied navigation as a POMDP and split it into five stages, Transition, Observation, Fusion, Reward-policy construction and Action (TOFRA), which map onto sensing, social and motion intelligence, and use these stages to organize the literature.
insight: Casting classic Bayesian filtering (transition, observation, fusion) and policy learning (reward-policy) in one POMDP shows where classic robotics and learning-based navigation overlap and where they differ. Each stage shows a similar trend from explicit, hand-designed models to implicit, adaptive or cognition-enhanced ones. This is a conceptual survey with no ablations or experiments. Its open problems are adaptive spatial-temporal scale, joint optimization of T/O/F/policy, system integrity, and generality across data and tasks (sim-to-real).
method: POMDP formulation: belief b(s_t), transition T, observation O, fusion F, reward R and policy π; the objective is to maximize expected discounted reward over the belief.

Prerequisites (state and action spaces): state representations (vector, Lie group, quaternion, implicit/neural, graph) and action spaces (wheeled, UAV/AUV, legged, wheel-legged; low-level vs high-level commands).

Sensing intelligence (T, O, F): dynamics-based dead reckoning, activity-recognition-enhanced and end-to-end transition; low-level feature, high-level cognitive and multi-agent observation; Kalman, optimization, neural and hybrid fusion.
Social intelligence (R): single-task (point, image, object goal, exploration), multi-task and language-instructed (VLN, LLM, RAG) reward-policy construction.
Motion intelligence (A): meta skills, combination skills (sequential composition, leg-arm manipulation) and morphological collaboration (wheel-legged, terrestrial-aerial, aerial-aquatic).

Systems, platforms and metrics: full-pipeline systems for autonomous driving, indoor and terrain navigation; simulators and real robots; social (SR, SPL, FLOPs, Coverage), sensing (ATE, RTE, NEES, map metrics) and motion (energy, path deviation) metrics.

Open problems: adaptive spatial/temporal scale (module scheduling under compute constraints), joint optimization, integrity (quantifiable, explainable, alarm, anti-interference) and data/task generality.

setting.simulator: N/A (surveys AI2-THOR, Habitat, SAPIEN, iGibson, ThreeDWorld, GRUtopia)

numbers_note: Survey paper; no experimental results or benchmark numbers reported.
results: There are no experimental results. The contribution is the TOFRA framework, a categorization of methods across sensing, social and motion intelligence, and a comparison table showing that prior surveys each cover only part of these areas while this survey covers all of them.
limitations: Conceptual and qualitative only: no quantitative cross-method comparison or benchmark results table.
Coverage of the social-intelligence stage (VLN, ObjectNav, LLM navigation) is brief compared with the sensing stage; recent VLN/LLM-agent work is cited only in passing.
The unified POMDP is idealized: it treats language-goal tasks as a reward/policy problem and does not model instruction grounding explicitly.
